# test_clamp.py
import math
import pytest

from your_module import clamp     # replace `your_module` with the real module name


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Happy-path tests
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "value, min_val, max_val, expected",
    [
        # inside the interval
        (5, 0, 10, 5),
        (-5, -10, -1, -5),
        # exactly on the borders
        (0, 0, 10, 0),
        (10, 0, 10, 10),
        (-10, -10, -1, -10),
        (-1, -10, -1, -1),
        # outside the interval
        (-1, 0, 10, 0),      # below min
        (11, 0, 10, 10),     # above max
    ],
)
def test_clamp_happy_path(value, min_val, max_val, expected):
    assert clamp(value, min_val, max_val) == pytest.approx(expected)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Edge-case tests
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def test_clamp_with_infinities():
    assert clamp(float("inf"), 0, 10) == 10          # +∞ gets clamped down
    assert clamp(float("-inf"), 0, 10) == 0          # –∞ gets clamped up


def test_clamp_with_nan_returns_nan():
    """NaN propagates all the way through the implementation."""
    result = clamp(float("nan"), 0, 10)
    assert math.isnan(result)


def test_min_greater_than_max_documents_current_behaviour():
    """
    The implementation does *not* raise if the caller supplies an invalid range.
    It effectively returns `min_val`.
    """
    assert clamp(5, 10, 0) == 10


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Error-case tests
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "value, min_val, max_val",
    [
        ("not numeric", 0, 10),  # bad value
        (5, "not numeric", 10),  # bad min_val
        (5, 0, "not numeric"),   # bad max_val
    ],
)
def test_non_numeric_arguments_raise_type_error(value, min_val, max_val):
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        clamp(value, min_val, max_val)
